lanes.label: New heavens and a new earth
Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: Isaiah: overview
nodes.d: Isaiah son of Amoz sees visions concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah; the book moves from indictment and judgment to comfort, a servant, and new heavens and a new earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Isaiah was and describe, using Isaiah 1:1 and 40:1-2, how the book moves from rebuke to comfort?
ev: Name the four kings of Judah named in Isaiah 1:1
Describe the shift in tone between chapters 1-39 and chapter 40 using the texts

nodes.t: The Lord charges his rebellious children
nodes.d: The LORD calls heaven and earth to witness that the children he raised have rebelled, rejects their empty sacrifices, and offers cleansing if they are willing and obedient.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD says he is weary of sacrifices in Isaiah 1 and what he commands instead?
ev: Retell the charge of Isaiah 1:2-4
Explain why God rejects the sacrifices in 1:11-15 and what he asks instead in 1:16-17
Quote the offer in 1:18-20

nodes.t: The mountain of the Lord in the last days
nodes.d: Isaiah sees the mountain of the LORD's house raised up, nations streaming to learn his ways, and weapons turned into farming tools; the house of Jacob is called to walk in his light.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Isaiah 2:2-4 says will happen to the nations and to weapons in the last days?
ev: Describe what the nations say and do in Isaiah 2:2-4
Explain the image of swords into plowshares from the text

nodes.t: The day of the Lord humbles the proud
nodes.d: Judah is full of silver, horses and idols, and a day of the LORD is coming on everything lofty so that he alone is exalted and men are told to cease trusting in man.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the day of the LORD brings against the proud in Isaiah 2:12-17?
ev: List what Judah is full of in Isaiah 2:7-8
Say what the day of the LORD comes against (2:12-17)
Explain the command in 2:22

nodes.t: Jerusalem stripped of support
nodes.d: The Lord takes away Jerusalem's leaders and supplies, the people oppress one another, the elders and the proud daughters of Zion are charged, and the city is left desolate.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD takes from Jerusalem in Isaiah 3 and why?
ev: Name the supports taken away in Isaiah 3:1-3
Describe the LORD's charge against the elders in 3:14-15
Describe the fate of the haughty daughters of Zion (3:16-26)

nodes.t: The Branch of the Lord and the cleansed remnant
nodes.d: After judgment, the Branch of the LORD is beautiful and glorious, those left in Zion are called holy, and the LORD covers Zion with cloud by day and fire by night as a shelter.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the LORD does for Zion in Isaiah 4:2-6 after washing away her filth?
ev: Say who is called holy in Isaiah 4:3
Describe the cloud, fire and shelter over Zion in 4:5-6

nodes.t: The song of the vineyard
nodes.d: Isaiah sings of a beloved's well-tended vineyard that yields wild grapes, and the LORD explains that the vineyard is the house of Israel, for which he looked for justice and righteousness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the song of the vineyard and say what Isaiah 5:7 says it means?
ev: Retell what the owner did for the vineyard (5:1-2)
Say what he will do to it (5:5-6)
Explain who the vineyard is according to 5:7

nodes.t: Six woes and the distant nation
nodes.d: Isaiah pronounces woes on land-grabbers, drunkards, those who call evil good and those who pervert justice, and says the LORD will summon a swift nation from afar against his people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name at least three of the woes in Isaiah 5 and the reason given for judgment in 5:24?
ev: List the woes of Isaiah 5:8, 11, 18, 20, 21 and 22
Explain why the LORD's anger is not turned away (5:24-25)

nodes.t: Isaiah sees the Lord and is sent
nodes.d: In the year King Uzziah died Isaiah sees the LORD enthroned with seraphim crying holy, is cleansed by a coal from the altar, volunteers, and is told to preach to a people who will not understand until a stump remains.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Isaiah's vision in chapter 6, including what the seraphim cry and how Isaiah is cleansed?
ev: Retell what the seraphim say and do (6:2-7)
Explain Isaiah's response in 6:5 and 6:8
Describe the message he is given and the "holy seed" in 6:9-13

nodes.t: The sign of Immanuel to Ahaz
nodes.d: When Syria and Ephraim threaten Judah, Isaiah tells Ahaz to trust the LORD, Ahaz refuses to ask a sign, and the Lord gives a sign of a son called Immanuel, with Assyria coming on the land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the setting of Isaiah 7:14 and what Ahaz was told to do in 7:4-9?
ev: Explain what Rezin and Pekah plan against Judah (7:1-6)
Quote the sign in 7:14 and say to whom the word is addressed (7:13)
Describe the coming of the king of Assyria (7:17-20)

nodes.t: Maher-shalal-hash-baz and the Assyrian flood
nodes.d: Isaiah writes a name-sign for a son, the LORD warns that the king of Assyria will flood Judah, tells Isaiah not to fear what the people fear, and calls him to the law and testimony instead of mediums.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD says to sanctify him rather than fear what the people fear in Isaiah 8:11-13?
ev: Explain the meaning of the child's name sign in 8:1-4
Say whom Isaiah is told to fear and sanctify (8:12-13)
Explain the contrast between the law and testimony and consulting the dead (8:19-20)

nodes.t: Light for the people in darkness and the child born
nodes.d: Light shines on the people in darkness in Zebulun and Naphtali, the yoke is broken, and a child is born whose government, names and everlasting reign are on the throne of David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Isaiah 9:6-7 says about the child and the throne of David?
ev: Name the regions mentioned in Isaiah 9:1
List the names given to the child in 9:6
Explain what 9:7 says about his throne and kingdom

nodes.t: His hand is stretched out still
nodes.d: A refrain runs through four stanzas: Ephraim's pride, unrepentant people, false leaders and civil strife bring judgment, and the LORD's anger is not turned away; woe is also pronounced on unjust decrees.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} find the refrain repeated in Isaiah 9:8-10:4 and explain why the people are judged?
ev: Find the repeated refrain in Isaiah 9:12, 17, 21 and 10:4
Say what Ephraim's boast in 9:10 shows about the people's attitude

nodes.t: Assyria the rod, then judged
nodes.d: The LORD sends Assyria as the rod of his anger against a hypocritical nation, but punishes the king of Assyria for his boasting; a remnant will return and Zion is told not to fear.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the picture of the axe boasting against the one who swings it in Isaiah 10:15?
ev: Explain how Assyria is both used and judged (10:5-7, 12-15)
Say what is promised to the remnant (10:20-23)
Describe the comfort given to Zion in 10:24-27

nodes.t: The shoot from the stem of Jesse
nodes.d: A shoot from Jesse's stem, endowed with the Spirit of the LORD, judges the poor with righteousness; peace reaches even the animals, the earth is full of the knowledge of the LORD, and the remnant is gathered.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the one who comes from the stem of Jesse and the peace of his kingdom in Isaiah 11?
ev: List the gifts of the Spirit resting on him in Isaiah 11:2
Describe how he judges (11:3-5)
Describe the peaceful creation in 11:6-9 and the gathering in 11:10-12

nodes.t: A song of salvation
nodes.d: In that day the redeemed will praise the LORD, saying God is their salvation and strength, draw water from the wells of salvation, and call all the earth to sing.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the people sing in Isaiah 12 and why they can praise the LORD?
ev: Quote the declaration of trust in Isaiah 12:2
Say what the people are told to do in 12:4-6

nodes.t: The burden of Babylon and the fallen king
nodes.d: The LORD musters an army against Babylon, a day of the LORD brings desolation by the Medes, and a taunt song mocks the king of Babylon who said he would ascend and be like the Most High.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the proverb against the king of Babylon in Isaiah 14:4-20?
ev: Name the people the LORD stirs up against Babylon (13:17)
Describe the king's boast and his fall in 14:12-15
Say what mercy the LORD shows Jacob in 14:1-3

nodes.t: The LORD's purpose against Assyria and Philistia
nodes.d: The LORD swears to break Assyria on his mountains, declares his purpose stretched over all nations, and tells Philistia not to rejoice, since Zion is founded by the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD says in Isaiah 14:24-27 about his purpose?
ev: Say what the LORD has sworn about Assyria (14:24-25)
Quote the answer to the messengers in 14:32

nodes.t: The burden of Moab
nodes.d: Moab is laid waste in a night and mourns, a request is made for Moab's outcasts to find shelter in Judah where a throne is established in mercy, and Moab's pride is judged with a time limit.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Isaiah 15-16 portrays Moab's fall and the grief it causes?
ev: Describe the mourning of Moab (15:2-5)
Say what is said of the throne in 16:5
Identify the time limit given in 16:14

nodes.t: Damascus, Israel and the land beyond Ethiopia
nodes.d: Damascus becomes a ruin and Ephraim's fortress ceases, a remnant turns to its Maker, and the roaring nations are rebuked; Ethiopia is addressed and a gift is brought to the LORD at Zion.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the burden of Damascus and the reason given in Isaiah 17:10?
ev: Say why Ephraim is judged according to Isaiah 17:10
Describe the fate of the roaring nations (17:12-14)
Say what happens to Ethiopia's people in 18:7

nodes.t: The burden of Egypt and Isaiah's sign
nodes.d: The LORD comes against Egypt, whose counsel fails; yet he promises that Egypt will know and serve him, and that Egypt, Assyria and Israel will be a blessing; Isaiah walks barefoot as a sign against trusting Egypt and Ethiopia.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Isaiah 19:19-25 says will happen to Egypt and what Isaiah's sign in chapter 20 means?
ev: Describe the judgment on Egypt (19:1-15)
Describe the blessing on Egypt, Assyria and Israel (19:23-25)
Explain what Isaiah's walking naked and barefoot signifies (20:2-6)

nodes.t: Babylon's fall, Dumah and Arabia
nodes.d: Isaiah watches in fear at a grievous vision, the watchman announces that Babylon is fallen, Seir asks the watchman what remains of the night, and Arabia's glory is to fail within a year.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the watchman's report in Isaiah 21:6-9?
ev: Describe what the watchman reports in Isaiah 21:6-9
Say what the watchman answers in 21:11-12

nodes.t: The valley of vision and Shebna
nodes.d: Jerusalem is distressed by a day of trouble; the people prepare defenses but do not look to the LORD and say let us eat and drink; Shebna is removed and Eliakim receives the key of the house of David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jerusalem does in Isaiah 22:8-13 and what the LORD says about it?
ev: Say what the people do and fail to do in Isaiah 22:8-13
Explain what happens to Shebna and Eliakim (22:15-25)

nodes.t: The burden of Tyre
nodes.d: Tyre, the merchant city, is laid waste by the LORD's purpose, forgotten seventy years, and afterward returns to her trade, which will be holy to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Isaiah 23 says about Tyre's fall and her trade after seventy years?
ev: Say who purposed Tyre's fall and why (23:9)
Describe what happens after seventy years (23:15-18)

nodes.t: The LORD lays waste the earth
nodes.d: The LORD empties the earth because its people broke the laws and the everlasting covenant; joy ceases, the earth reels, the host on high and kings below are punished, and the LORD reigns in Zion.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the earth is emptied in Isaiah 24 and who reigns at the end?
ev: Say why the earth is defiled (24:5)
Describe the punishment of the host on high and the kings of the earth (24:21-22)
Say where the LORD reigns (24:23)

nodes.t: A feast on the mountain and death swallowed up
nodes.d: The LORD makes a feast for all peoples on his mountain, removes the veil over all nations, swallows up death, wipes away tears, and the redeemed say they waited for him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD does for all peoples on his mountain in Isaiah 25:6-9?
ev: Describe the feast and the veil (25:6-7)
Quote what the LORD does to death and tears (25:8)
Say what the people say in 25:9

nodes.t: A song in Judah: perfect peace and the dead who live
nodes.d: Judah sings of a strong city and perfect peace for those who trust the LORD, laments that they have brought no deliverance, and hears that the LORD's dead shall live and the earth will disclose her slain.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Isaiah 26:3 and 26:19 promise?
ev: Quote the promise of peace in Isaiah 26:3
Say what is promised about the dead in 26:19
Describe the call to hide until the indignation is past (26:20-21)

nodes.t: Leviathan punished and the vineyard of red wine
nodes.d: The LORD punishes leviathan, the vineyard he guards will fill the world with fruit, Jacob's iniquity is purged, and the scattered are gathered with a great trumpet to worship at Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the vineyard of Isaiah 27 and compare it with the vineyard in Isaiah 5?
ev: Say what the LORD does to leviathan (27:1)
Describe the vineyard and its keeper (27:2-6)
Describe the gathering in 27:12-13

nodes.t: Woe to Ephraim's drunkards and the scoffers in Jerusalem
nodes.d: Isaiah rebukes the drunken leaders, who mock his teaching, boast of a covenant with death, and are promised a tested cornerstone laid in Zion; the farmer's patient work illustrates God's wise ways.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the scoffers in Isaiah 28:15 relied on and what the LORD lays in Zion in 28:16?
ev: Describe the scoffers' covenant with death (28:15)
Quote what the LORD lays in Zion (28:16)
Explain the farmer illustration in 28:23-29

nodes.t: Woe to Ariel: a sealed vision and a marvellous work
nodes.d: The LORD besieges Ariel, the city where David dwelt, then saves it from the nations; the people honour him with lips but not hearts, the vision is like a sealed book, and the deaf will hear and the blind see.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what 29:13 says about the people's worship?
ev: Describe the siege and sudden deliverance of Ariel (29:1-8)
Explain the charge in 29:13
Describe the change promised in 29:17-24

nodes.t: Rebellious children and trust in Egypt
nodes.d: Judah sends to Egypt for help instead of asking the LORD, refuses to hear true prophecy, and is told that in returning and rest is salvation; the LORD will wait to be gracious and will beat down Assyria.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the people were told in Isaiah 30:15 and how they answered?
ev: Say why the LORD calls the people rebellious (30:1-2, 9-11)
Quote 30:15 and the people's answer in 30:16
Describe the grace promised in 30:18-26

nodes.t: Woe to those who trust in horses
nodes.d: Those who go to Egypt for help trust in chariots rather than the LORD, who is wise and will protect Jerusalem like birds flying; Assyria will fall by a sword not of man.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast Egypt's horses with the LORD's help in Isaiah 31:1-3?
ev: Say what the people trust instead of the LORD (31:1)
Quote the contrast in 31:3
Describe how the LORD defends Jerusalem (31:4-5)

nodes.t: A king reigns in righteousness; the Spirit is poured out
nodes.d: A king and princes will reign in righteousness, careless women are warned of coming desolation, until the Spirit is poured from on high and righteousness and peace dwell in the land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what 32:15-17 says happens when the Spirit is poured out?
ev: Describe the king and the changes in 32:1-8
Say what ends the desolation (32:15)
Say what the work of righteousness is (32:17)

nodes.t: The destroyer destroyed and the LORD our king
nodes.d: The spoiler is warned, the people pray for grace, the LORD rises to be exalted, sinners in Zion fear the devouring fire, and the righteous see the king; the LORD is judge, lawgiver and king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say the three roles given to the LORD in Isaiah 33:22?
ev: Say who asks, "Who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire?" and the answer (33:14-16)
Quote 33:22
Describe Jerusalem as a quiet habitation (33:20)

nodes.t: The day of vengeance on the nations and Edom
nodes.d: The LORD's indignation is on all nations; his sword comes down on Edom for the controversy of Zion, and the land becomes a lasting wasteland inhabited by wild creatures.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Edom is singled out in Isaiah 34:5-8?
ev: Say what the LORD does to the host of heaven and the nations (34:2-4)
Say which land receives the sword (34:5-6)
Describe Edom after judgment (34:9-15)

nodes.t: The desert blooms and the way of holiness
nodes.d: The wilderness blossoms, the weak are strengthened, the blind see and the lame leap, and a highway of holiness leads the ransomed to Zion with everlasting joy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the way of holiness and the people who walk it in Isaiah 35?
ev: Describe the healings in Isaiah 35:5-6
Say who walks the way of holiness (35:8-10)

nodes.t: Sennacherib's envoy mocks Jerusalem
nodes.d: In Hezekiah's fourteenth year Sennacherib's envoy Rabshakeh stands by Jerusalem's conduit and tries to turn the people from trusting Hezekiah and the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Rabshakeh says to Jerusalem's people in Isaiah 36 and how they answer?
ev: Retell the arguments Rabshakeh uses (36:4-10, 14-20)
Say how Hezekiah's officers respond (36:21-22)

nodes.t: Hezekiah prays and the angel strikes the Assyrian camp
nodes.d: Hezekiah takes the letter to the LORD's house and prays; Isaiah answers that the LORD will defend Jerusalem, and the angel of the LORD strikes the Assyrian camp so that Sennacherib returns to Nineveh.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how the LORD answered Hezekiah's prayer in Isaiah 37?
ev: Retell Hezekiah's prayer (37:14-20)
Say what Isaiah's answer promises (37:21-35)
Retell what happens to Sennacherib (37:36-38)

nodes.t: Hezekiah's sickness and recovery
nodes.d: Hezekiah, told he will die, prays and weeps; the LORD adds fifteen years, promises to deliver the city from Assyria, and gives a sign with the shadow on the sundial; Hezekiah writes a thanksgiving.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how the LORD answered Hezekiah when he was sick in Isaiah 38?
ev: Retell what Isaiah first says to Hezekiah and how Hezekiah responds (38:1-3)
Say what the LORD adds and the sign given (38:5-8)
Describe the lesson of the writing in 38:17-20

nodes.t: Envoys from Babylon
nodes.d: Merodach-baladan sends letters to Hezekiah, who shows them all his treasures; Isaiah tells him everything will be carried to Babylon, and Hezekiah calls the word good because there will be peace in his days.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Isaiah told Hezekiah about Babylon and how Hezekiah answered?
ev: Say what Hezekiah shows the envoys (39:2)
Say what Isaiah foretells (39:5-7)
Describe Hezekiah's response (39:8)

nodes.t: Comfort my people: the incomparable God
nodes.d: God tells his prophets to comfort Jerusalem because her iniquity is pardoned, a voice prepares the way of the LORD, the LORD comes as shepherd, and no one compares to him who gives strength to the weary.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD comforts Jerusalem in Isaiah 40:1-2 and who the LORD is compared to in 40:12-26?
ev: Quote the command and reason in Isaiah 40:1-2
Describe the voice crying in the wilderness (40:3-5)
Explain what 40:28-31 says about those who wait on the LORD

nodes.t: The LORD chose Israel; idols have no answer
nodes.d: The LORD calls Israel his servant, the seed of Abraham his friend, and tells them not to fear; he challenges the idols to declare the future and raises up one from the north and east.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD tells Israel in Isaiah 41:8-10 and how he challenges the idols?
ev: Quote the promise in Isaiah 41:10
Say how Israel is addressed in 41:8-14
Describe the challenge to the idols (41:21-29)

nodes.t: Behold my servant
nodes.d: The LORD presents his chosen servant, on whom he puts his Spirit, who brings justice to the nations gently and is given as a covenant and a light to the Gentiles to open blind eyes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the servant and his work in Isaiah 42:1-7?
ev: List what the LORD says of the servant (42:1-4)
Say what the servant is given for (42:6-7)
Explain 42:8 about the LORD's glory

nodes.t: A new song and the blind servant
nodes.d: The LORD is called to be praised to the ends of the earth and goes forth as a warrior, but his servant is blind and deaf; Jacob was given to plunder because they would not walk in his ways.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD calls his servant blind and deaf in Isaiah 42:18-25?
ev: Describe the new song and the LORD as a warrior (42:10-13)
Explain what is said of the blind and deaf servant (42:18-20)
Say why Jacob was given to spoil (42:24-25)

nodes.t: I have redeemed you; I am the LORD, your Saviour
nodes.d: The LORD redeems and calls Jacob by name, will be with them through waters and fire, gathers sons from the ends of the earth, calls Israel his witnesses, does a new thing, and blots out their transgressions for his own sake.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD promises in Isaiah 43:1-2 and 43:25?
ev: Quote the promise in Isaiah 43:1-2
Say what Israel is called in 43:10-12
Explain the "new thing" (43:18-19) and the forgiveness in 43:25

nodes.t: The folly of idols and the Spirit poured out
nodes.d: The LORD pours his Spirit on Jacob's seed and declares he is first and last with no God beside him, while the idol-maker's craft is shown to be foolish; the LORD blots out transgressions.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Isaiah 44:9-20 calls idol-making foolish?
ev: Quote 44:6
Describe how the idol is made and used (44:12-17)
Say what the LORD says to Israel in 44:21-22

nodes.t: Cyrus, the LORD's shepherd and anointed
nodes.d: The LORD names Cyrus, by name before his time, as his shepherd and anointed who will let Jerusalem and the temple be rebuilt, so that all will know there is none else.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD says Cyrus will do and why in Isaiah 44:28-45:6?
ev: Say what the LORD says of Cyrus (44:28, 45:1)
Explain why the LORD calls Cyrus by name (45:4-6)
Quote the invitation in 45:22-23

nodes.t: Babylon's gods carried, Israel carried by God
nodes.d: Bel and Nebo are carried off as burdens while the LORD has carried Israel from birth and to old age; he declares the end from the beginning.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast the gods of Babylon with the LORD in Isaiah 46:1-4?
ev: Contrast who carries whom in Isaiah 46:1-4
Say what the LORD declares in 46:9-10

nodes.t: The fall of Babylon the lady of kingdoms
nodes.d: The virgin daughter of Babylon is brought down from her throne, for she showed the LORD's people no mercy and trusted in sorceries and in saying "I am, and none else"; her counsellors cannot save her.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Babylon is brought low in Isaiah 47?
ev: Say why Babylon is judged (47:6-8)
Describe what her sorceries and astrologers cannot do (47:12-15)

nodes.t: The obstinate house of Jacob and the furnace of affliction
nodes.d: The LORD tells Jacob he foretold things because they were obstinate, delays his anger for his name's sake, calls them out of Babylon, and says had they heeded his commandments their peace would be like a river.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD says he tested Israel in the furnace of affliction in Isaiah 48:10-11?
ev: Say why the LORD declared things beforehand (48:3-7)
Describe the call to leave Babylon (48:20-21)
Quote 48:22

nodes.t: The servant, a light to the nations
nodes.d: The servant called from the womb, whose mouth is like a sharp sword, says he has laboured in vain; the LORD says it is too light a thing to restore Israel and gives him as a light to the Gentiles, and promises Zion she is not forgotten.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD says is "too light a thing" for his servant in Isaiah 49:6?
ev: Describe how the servant is called (49:1-3)
Quote the LORD's answer in 49:6
Say what the LORD says to Zion in 49:14-16

nodes.t: The servant who gives his back to the smiters
nodes.d: The servant says the Lord GOD opened his ear and he was not rebellious, gave his back to those who struck him, and sets his face like flint trusting the Lord's help; those who walk in darkness are urged to trust the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the servant says he will endure and why he is not put to shame in Isaiah 50:4-9?
ev: Describe what the servant endures (50:5-6)
Say why he is not ashamed (50:7-9)

nodes.t: Awake, arm of the LORD
nodes.d: Those who pursue righteousness are told to look to Abraham and Sarah, the LORD promises comfort and a law going forth, the arm of the LORD is called to awake as in ancient days, and Jerusalem is told the cup of fury is taken from her.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who the people are told to look to in Isaiah 51:1-2 and why?
ev: Say whom they are told to look to (51:1-2)
Describe the cry to the arm of the LORD (51:9-11)
Say what happens to the cup of trembling (51:22-23)

nodes.t: Awake, Zion: good tidings of peace
nodes.d: Jerusalem is told to put on strength, she is redeemed without money, the feet of the one who brings good tidings are beautiful, and the LORD has bared his arm before the nations.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what 52:7 describes about the one who brings good tidings?
ev: Quote 52:7
Say what the watchmen see (52:8)
Describe the command to depart in 52:11-12

nodes.t: The servant exalted, despised and bearing iniquity
nodes.d: The servant is high, yet marred; despised and rejected, he bears griefs and iniquities of others, is wounded for transgressions and led like a lamb, is cut off and buried with the rich, and after his soul's travail justifies many.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the servant suffers and for whose sake according to Isaiah 53:4-6?
ev: Describe what Isaiah 53:4-6 says he bears and for whom
Describe how he is treated (53:3, 7-9)
Say what the LORD says follows in 53:10-12

nodes.t: Sing, barren one: the covenant of peace
nodes.d: The barren woman is told to sing and enlarge her tent, the LORD her husband has called her back with mercy, swears as with the waters of Noah, and promises a covenant of peace that will not be removed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the LORD compares his promise in Isaiah 54:9-10 to the waters of Noah?
ev: Describe the call to the barren woman (54:1-3)
Say what the LORD compares his oath to (54:9)
Quote the promise in 54:10

nodes.t: Come, buy without money: the sure mercies of David
nodes.d: The LORD invites the thirsty to come without money, promises an everlasting covenant, the sure mercies of David, calls the wicked to return, and says his word will accomplish what he pleases.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who is invited and what is promised in Isaiah 55:1-7?
ev: Quote the invitation in Isaiah 55:1-3
Say what is promised to those who return (55:7)
Explain 55:10-11

nodes.t: Foreigners and eunuchs welcomed; blind watchmen
nodes.d: The LORD says foreigners and eunuchs who hold to his covenant and keep sabbaths will be joyful in his house of prayer for all peoples, while blind watchmen and greedy shepherds are condemned.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who the LORD welcomes in Isaiah 56:3-8 and what his house is called?
ev: Say who is welcomed in Isaiah 56:3-7
Quote what the house is called (56:7)
Describe the charge against the watchmen (56:10-12)

nodes.t: Idolatry condemned; the LORD revives the contrite
nodes.d: The perishing of the righteous goes unnoticed, the idolatrous are condemned, and the high and lofty One who inhabits eternity dwells with the contrite and heals; there is no peace for the wicked.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say with whom the LORD dwells in Isaiah 57:15?
ev: Describe the idolatry condemned in Isaiah 57:3-10
Say whom the LORD dwells with in 57:15
Quote 57:21

nodes.t: The fast the LORD chooses
nodes.d: The people fast yet oppress, and the LORD says the fast he chooses is to loose bonds, share bread with the hungry and clothe the naked, promising light and healing; he also promises delight to those who honour the sabbath.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the fast the LORD chooses in Isaiah 58:6-7?
ev: Explain what is wrong with the people's fast (58:3-5)
List the fast the LORD chooses (58:6-7)
Describe the promises that follow (58:8-12)

nodes.t: Your iniquities have separated; the Redeemer comes
nodes.d: The LORD's hand is not short, but iniquities separate the people from God; he sees no intercessor, so his own arm brings salvation, and the Redeemer comes to Zion with a covenant that his Spirit and words will not depart.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what has separated the people from God in Isaiah 59:1-2 and how the LORD responds?
ev: Quote Isaiah 59:1-2
List sins in 59:3-8
Say what the LORD does when he sees no intercessor (59:16-17) and the covenant of 59:21

nodes.t: Arise, shine: the glory of Zion
nodes.d: Zion's light has come and nations and kings come to her brightness with gifts, her walls are Salvation and her gates Praise, and the LORD himself is her everlasting light.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what happens to Zion and what her light is in Isaiah 60?
ev: Say what comes to Zion (60:3-9)
Say what replaces sun and moon (60:19-20)
Describe the people (60:21)

nodes.t: The Spirit is upon me: good tidings to the meek
nodes.d: A speaker anointed by the Spirit proclaims good tidings to the poor and release for captives, the year of the LORD's favour and a day of vengeance, and the mourners are given beauty for ashes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what the one anointed by the Spirit proclaims in Isaiah 61:1-3?
ev: List what the anointed one announces in Isaiah 61:1-3
Say what the people are called in 61:6
Describe the everlasting covenant in 61:8-9

nodes.t: A new name for Zion
nodes.d: The LORD will not rest until Zion's righteousness shines, calls her by a new name, rejoices over her like a bridegroom, sets watchmen on her walls, and calls her people the holy people and the redeemed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Zion is called and how the LORD feels about her in Isaiah 62?
ev: Describe the new names (62:2-4, 12)
Quote the picture in 62:5
Say what the watchmen do (62:6-7)

nodes.t: One comes from Edom with red garments
nodes.d: A glorious figure from Edom with garments stained from the winepress declares he trod the peoples alone in anger, for the day of vengeance and the year of his redeemed has come.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the figure in Isaiah 63:1-6 and what he has done?
ev: Describe the figure and his garments (63:1-3)
Say why he acts alone (63:5)

nodes.t: A prayer of remembrance and lament
nodes.d: The prophet recalls the LORD's kindnesses and how Israel rebelled and he became their enemy, then prays for him to look down and come down, confessing sin, and says "we are the clay and thou our potter."
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the prayer of Isaiah 63:15-64:12 and what the people confess?
ev: Recall what the LORD did for his people (63:7-14)
Quote the confession in 64:6
Quote 64:8

nodes.t: New heavens and a new earth
nodes.d: The LORD answers a rebellious people, saves a remnant of his servants, and creates new heavens and a new earth and Jerusalem a joy where weeping is no more and the wolf and lamb feed together.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the LORD says he will create in Isaiah 65:17-25?
ev: Say who the LORD preserves and who he judges (65:8-15)
Describe the new heavens and new earth (65:17-25)

nodes.t: Heaven my throne: the final word
nodes.d: The LORD asks where a house can be built for him who made all things and looks to the humble and contrite; he comforts Jerusalem, comes with fire, gathers all nations to see his glory, and the new heavens and earth remain.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say whom the LORD looks to in Isaiah 66:2 and how the book ends?
ev: Say whom the LORD looks to (66:2)
Describe the gathering of the nations (66:18-21)
Describe the end in 66:22-24

nodes.t: Matthew: overview
nodes.d: The gospel of Matthew, from the genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David and son of Abraham (1:1), through the five great discourses, the passion and the resurrection, to the closing commission (28:16-20).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Matthew is about and how it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: birth and preparation (1-4), the Sermon on the Mount (5-7), miracles and mission (8-12), parables of the kingdom (13), teaching on the way to Jerusalem (14-23), the coming kingdom (24-25), the passion and resurrection (26-28)
Name where the book starts and ends

nodes.t: The birth of Jesus announced to Joseph
nodes.d: Joseph finds Mary with child by the Holy Ghost, and an angel tells him in a dream to take her as wife and name the child Jesus, who will save his people from their sins.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Joseph was told in his dream and why the child was named Jesus?
ev: Retell what the angel told Joseph
Say what the name Jesus is linked to in 1:21

nodes.t: John the Baptist prepares the way
nodes.d: John preaches repentance in the wilderness, baptizes in the Jordan, warns Pharisees and Sadducees to bear fruit, and says one mightier will baptize with the Holy Ghost and fire.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what John the Baptist told people to do and who he said was coming?
ev: Say what John preached
Explain the difference John draws between his baptism and the coming one’s

nodes.t: Jesus begins in Galilee and calls fishermen
nodes.d: Hearing John is imprisoned, Jesus moves to Capernaum, preaches repentance for the kingdom of heaven, calls Peter, Andrew, James and John from their nets, and heals great crowds.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jesus called his first disciples?
ev: Name the four fishermen Jesus called
Summarise what Jesus did throughout Galilee (4:23-25)

nodes.t: Healing Peter’s mother-in-law and many others
nodes.d: Jesus heals Peter’s wife’s mother of a fever and, that evening, casts out spirits and heals all who are brought; Matthew links this to a word of Isaiah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Jesus did in Peter’s house and that evening?
ev: Retell the healing in Peter’s house
Say what Matthew says was fulfilled in 8:17

nodes.t: Healing the withered hand and the chosen servant
nodes.d: In the synagogue Jesus heals a man’s withered hand on the sabbath after saying it is lawful to do good; the Pharisees plot, and Matthew says his gentle ministry fulfils Isaiah’s word of the chosen servant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus healed on the sabbath and what the Pharisees planned?
ev: Retell the healing and the reason Jesus gave
Say what the Pharisees did next

nodes.t: The parable of the sower
nodes.d: Jesus tells of seed falling on the path, stony ground, thorns and good ground, explains why he speaks in parables, and interprets the sower for his disciples.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what each soil in the parable stands for?
ev: Retell the four soils
Give the explanation Jesus gave for each

nodes.t: Tradition and what defiles
nodes.d: Pharisees accuse the disciples of breaking the tradition of the elders; Jesus charges them with voiding God’s commandment by tradition and says what comes out of the heart, not what goes into the mouth, defiles.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said defiles a person?
ev: Give Jesus’ example of tradition overriding a commandment
List what comes out of the heart (15:19)

nodes.t: Jesus enters Jerusalem
nodes.d: Jesus sends two disciples for an ass and colt, and rides toward Jerusalem while crowds spread garments and branches and cry Hosanna to the son of David; Matthew says this fulfils a word about the King coming meek on an ass.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Jesus came into Jerusalem and what the crowds said?
ev: Describe the entry
Say what the crowds shouted

nodes.t: Cleansing the temple
nodes.d: Jesus drives out the buyers and sellers, overturns tables and seats, says the house of prayer has become a den of thieves, heals the blind and lame, and answers the priests about children’s praise.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus overturned the tables?
ev: Say what Jesus did and quoted
Describe what the children cried and the priests’ reaction

nodes.t: The parable of the wicked tenants
nodes.d: Tenants of a vineyard beat and kill the owner’s servants and then his son; Jesus cites the rejected stone made head of the corner, says the kingdom will be taken from them, and the priests perceive he speaks of them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who the servants, son and tenants stand for in the parable?
ev: Retell the parable
Say what the priests understood

nodes.t: Mark: overview
nodes.d: The gospel of Mark, from “the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God” (1:1) through Jesus’ ministry in Galilee, the road to Jerusalem and his death, to the empty tomb and commission.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Mark is about and where it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: John and the start of ministry (1), Galilee (1-8), the way to Jerusalem (8-10), the last week and passion (11-15), the empty tomb (16)
Say what Mark calls the book in 1:1

nodes.t: John prepares the way
nodes.d: Mark opens with the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God; John baptizes in the wilderness for repentance and says one mightier will baptize with the Holy Ghost.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who John was and what he said about the one coming after him?
ev: Say how Mark begins his book
Describe John’s message and appearance

nodes.t: Tradition of the elders and what defiles
nodes.d: Pharisees fault the disciples for eating with unwashed hands; Jesus quotes Isaiah on lip service, charges them with setting aside God’s commandment through Corban, and says what comes out of the heart defiles.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says defiles a person?
ev: Explain Jesus’ Corban example
List what proceeds from the heart (7:21-22)

nodes.t: The fig tree and the cleansing of the temple
nodes.d: Jesus curses a leafy fig tree without fruit, drives out sellers and moneychangers saying the house is for prayer for all nations, and next day the disciples see the fig tree withered; he teaches faith and forgiving when praying.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus did in the temple and what he taught about prayer?
ev: Retell the order of events
Say what Jesus taught about prayer

nodes.t: The parable of the vineyard tenants
nodes.d: A man plants a vineyard and lets it to husbandmen who beat and kill his servants and then his beloved son; Jesus cites the rejected stone that became head of the corner, and the rulers know the parable is against them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who the servants, son and husbandmen stand for?
ev: Retell the parable
Say what the rulers understood

nodes.t: Luke: The Gospel Orderly Told
nodes.d: Luke writes an orderly account for Theophilus so he may know the certainty of what he was taught, from the births of John and Jesus to the resurrection, ascension and the apostles' commission.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Luke wrote his Gospel and where it begins and ends?
ev: Say who Luke addresses, why he wrote, and how the book begins and ends.

nodes.t: John the Baptist Prepares the Way
nodes.d: In the fifteenth year of Tiberius the word comes to John, who preaches a baptism of repentance, calls for fruits worthy of repentance, answers the crowds, tax collectors and soldiers, points to one mightier, and is imprisoned by Herod.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain John's message of repentance and what he said about the one coming after him?
ev: List what John told the crowds, tax collectors and soldiers to do and what he said about the coming one.

nodes.t: Jesus Reads Isaiah at Nazareth
nodes.d: In the Nazareth synagogue Jesus reads the passage about the anointed preacher of good news and says it is fulfilled in their hearing; he points to Elias and Eliseus helping outsiders, and the crowd tries to throw him down.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus read in Nazareth and why the people were angry?
ev: Say what Jesus read, what he said about it, and why the people turned on him.

nodes.t: Jesus Drives Out the Traders
nodes.d: Jesus enters the temple and drives out those selling, saying his house is a house of prayer but they made it a den of thieves, and teaches there daily while the chief priests seek to destroy him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Jesus did in the temple and what he said about it?
ev: Say what Jesus did in the temple and what he said.

nodes.t: Who Is Greatest: One Who Serves
nodes.d: The disciples dispute who is greatest; Jesus contrasts Gentile kings with himself as one who serves, promises them a kingdom, tells Simon that Satan desired to sift him but he prayed for his faith, and foretells Peter's three denials.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' teaching on greatness and his words to Peter?
ev: Say what Jesus said about greatness and what he told Peter.

nodes.t: John: Believe That Jesus Is the Christ
nodes.d: John presents Jesus as the Word made flesh through signs, 'I am' sayings, a farewell discourse, the cross and resurrection, and states that these things are written so readers believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and have life in his name.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why John wrote his Gospel and how it begins and ends?
ev: State why John says he wrote the book and name some signs or 'I am' sayings.

nodes.t: John the Baptist's Witness
nodes.d: Priests and Levites ask John who he is; he says he is not the Christ but a voice crying in the wilderness, and next day he sees Jesus and calls him the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world and the Son of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how John described himself and what he called Jesus?
ev: Say who John said he was and what he called Jesus.

nodes.t: Eat My Flesh, Drink My Blood
nodes.d: The Jews murmur that Jesus said he came down from heaven; he says no man comes unless the Father draws him, and that unless they eat his flesh and drink his blood they have no life; he contrasts himself with the manna their fathers ate.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says in John 6 about the Father drawing and about eating his flesh?
ev: Say what Jesus says about the Father's drawing and about eating his flesh and drinking his blood.

nodes.t: Unbelief and Jesus' Final Public Words
nodes.d: Despite many signs the people do not believe, which John says fulfils Isaiah, and many rulers believe but fear confessing him; Jesus cries that believing in him is believing in the one who sent him and that he came as light, not to judge but to save.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what John says about unbelief and what Jesus says about his words and judgment?
ev: Say why John says the people did not believe and what Jesus says about those who hear and reject his words.

nodes.t: Acts: overview
nodes.d: Acts continues Luke's account from the ascension of Jesus (1:9) to Paul preaching at Rome (28:31): the Holy Ghost at Pentecost, the church in Jerusalem, the witness spreading to Judaea, Samaria and the Gentiles, and Paul's journeys, arrest and voyage to Rome.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline how the gospel spreads in Acts from Jerusalem to Rome?
ev: Say how Acts 1:8 gives the shape of the book (Jerusalem, Judaea, Samaria, the uttermost part)
Name the major sections: Peter in Jerusalem, Stephen and Philip, Saul's conversion, Cornelius, Paul's journeys, Paul's arrest and Rome

nodes.t: Stephen's speech: tabernacle, temple and stiffnecked people
nodes.d: Stephen recalls the tabernacle in the wilderness and David and Solomon's house, then says the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands. He charges the council with resisting the Holy Ghost like their fathers, who persecuted the prophets and now betrayed and murdered the Just One.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Stephen answers the charge about the temple and what he accuses the council of?
ev: Say what Stephen says about where God dwells (7:48-50)
State the charge Stephen makes against the council (7:51-53)

nodes.t: Philip and the Ethiopian eunuch
nodes.d: An angel and the Spirit send Philip to a chariot on the road to Gaza, where an Ethiopian officer is reading Isaiah. Philip begins at that scripture and preaches Jesus; the man believes, is baptized, and goes on his way rejoicing.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Philip explained the scripture to the Ethiopian and what happened afterward?
ev: Say what the eunuch was reading and what Philip did with it (8:28-35)
Describe the baptism and what happened to Philip (8:36-40)

nodes.t: Paul preaches in the synagogue at Pisidian Antioch
nodes.d: Invited to speak after the reading of the law and prophets, Paul traces Israel's story from Egypt through the judges and David to Jesus, whom God raised from the dead. He declares forgiveness of sins and that by Jesus all who believe are justified from what the law of Moses could not justify.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarise Paul's sermon from Israel's history to forgiveness through Jesus?
ev: Outline the history Paul recounts to reach Jesus (13:17-23)
State what Paul says is preached through Jesus (13:38-39)

nodes.t: Paul and Barnabas turn to the Gentiles
nodes.d: Gentiles ask to hear more, and the next sabbath almost the whole city gathers; the envious Jews contradict, so Paul and Barnabas say they turn to the Gentiles, citing the Lord's command to be a light to them. The Gentiles rejoice, those ordained to eternal life believe, and the apostles are expelled.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul and Barnabas turned to the Gentiles at Antioch?
ev: Say why Paul and Barnabas turned to the Gentiles (13:45-47)
Describe how the Gentiles and the disciples responded (13:48, 13:52)

nodes.t: Paul preaches in Rome
nodes.d: Paul tells the Jewish leaders at Rome that he is bound for the hope of Israel and expounds the kingdom of God from Moses and the prophets, with some believing and others not. He quotes Isaiah on hardened hearts, says salvation is sent to the Gentiles, and for two years receives all who come, preaching with all confidence, no man forbidding him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul did and said at Rome and how Acts ends?
ev: Say how the Jews divided in response (28:24-25)
Describe how the book ends (28:30-31)

nodes.t: Romans: overview
nodes.d: Paul's letter to the Romans, from the greeting and the gospel theme (1:1-17) to its closing greetings and doxology (16:27).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Romans is about, using 1:16-17?
ev: State the letter's theme from 1:16-17
Describe the movement: sin (1-3), justification (3-5), life in Christ and the Spirit (6-8), Israel (9-11), Christian living (12-16)

nodes.t: God's sovereign election
nodes.d: Paul answers the question of Israel by pointing to God's sovereign choice, from Isaac and Jacob onward, and his mercy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Romans 9 says about God's choice and mercy?
ev: Link 9:7 to Genesis 21:12 and 9:12 to Genesis 25:23
Explain 9:15-16

nodes.t: Faith comes by hearing
nodes.d: Righteousness is for everyone who believes; faith comes by hearing the word of Christ.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Romans 10:9-10 and 10:17?
ev: State 10:9-10
Explain 10:17

nodes.t: The remnant and the olive tree
nodes.d: God has not cast off his people; a remnant is saved by grace, and Gentiles are grafted into the olive tree.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the olive tree picture in Romans 11?
ev: Explain the olive tree illustration in 11:17-24
Say how the chapter ends (11:33-36)

nodes.t: The strong and the weak
nodes.d: Believers are to welcome one another, not judge over disputable matters, and seek the good of their neighbour.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul says to treat a brother who disagrees on disputable matters?
ev: Explain 14:1 and 14:17

nodes.t: Closing greetings and doxology
nodes.d: Paul's plans, personal greetings, a warning, and the closing benediction and doxology.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how Romans ends?
ev: Read the doxology (16:25-27)

nodes.t: 1 Corinthians: overview
nodes.d: Paul writes to the church at Corinth about divisions, sin in the church, questions they asked him, worship, the resurrection and the collection (1:1-16:24).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of 1 Corinthians and name three problems Paul corrects in the Corinthian church?
ev: Name the main problems Paul addresses: divisions, immorality, lawsuits, marriage, food offered to idols, the Lord's supper, gifts, the resurrection
Say who the letter is addressed to from 1:2

nodes.t: The cross: God's wisdom and power
nodes.d: Paul says the preaching of the cross looks foolish to those perishing but is the power of God to those being saved, and that God chose the weak and low so that no one may boast.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says the cross is God's wisdom and power, using 1 Corinthians 1:18-31?
ev: Contrast how the cross is seen by those perishing and by those saved (1:18)
List who God chose according to 1:26-29 and why (1:29)
Name what Christ is made to us (1:30)

nodes.t: The Spirit reveals God's hidden wisdom
nodes.d: Paul preached Christ crucified in weakness, and says the wisdom of God, hidden from this world's rulers, is revealed by the Spirit and understood only spiritually.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain, using 1 Corinthians 2, how a person comes to understand the things of God?
ev: State what Paul determined to know among the Corinthians (2:2)
Explain who knows the things of God and how we receive them (2:10-12)
Contrast the natural man and the spiritual person (2:14-15)

nodes.t: Tongues, prophecy and order in the assembly
nodes.d: Paul urges them to seek gifts that build up the church, especially prophecy, requires tongues to be interpreted, regulates speaking in turn, and ends by saying all things should be done decently and in order.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the purpose Paul gives for all speaking in church (14:26) and the rules in 1 Corinthians 14:27-33?
ev: Explain why Paul prefers prophecy in church (14:3-5)
State the rules for tongues and prophets (14:27-32)
Say why God is not the author of confusion (14:33)
Read 14:34-35 carefully and say what it commands about speaking in the churches

nodes.t: If Christ is not raised: the firstfruits
nodes.d: Paul argues that if there is no resurrection of the dead then Christ is not risen and faith is vain, but Christ is risen as the firstfruits, as Adam brought death and Christ brings life, until death is destroyed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the resurrection of Christ matters for the believer, using 1 Corinthians 15:12-22?
ev: List the consequences if Christ is not risen (15:14-19)
Explain Adam and Christ in 15:21-22
Say what the last enemy is (15:26)

nodes.t: The resurrection body and the victory over death
nodes.d: Paul answers how the dead are raised, with the picture of a seed, contrasts the natural and spiritual body and the first and last Adam, and describes believers being changed at the last trumpet with death swallowed up in victory.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Paul says will happen to the dead in Christ and to the living, using 1 Corinthians 15:42-58?
ev: Explain the seed picture (15:36-38)
Contrast sown and raised in 15:42-44
Explain how believers will be changed (15:51-53)
State the closing exhortation of 15:58

nodes.t: 2 Corinthians: overview
nodes.d: Paul's second letter to the Corinthians: comfort in affliction, the ministry of the new covenant and reconciliation, the collection for the saints, and a defence of his apostleship (1:1-13:14).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of 2 Corinthians and say what its three main parts are about?
ev: Name the main sections: comfort and ministry (1-7), the collection (8-9), Paul's defence of his apostleship (10-13)
Say what Paul tells the Corinthians about his sufferings

nodes.t: The inward man is renewed
nodes.d: Paul says that although the outward man perishes, the inward man is renewed day by day, and that light affliction produces an eternal weight of glory for those who look at the unseen.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul does not lose heart, using 2 Corinthians 4:16-18?
ev: Contrast the outward and inward man (4:16)
Contrast the seen and the unseen (4:18)

nodes.t: New creation and the ministry of reconciliation
nodes.d: Paul says the love of Christ constrains us because he died for all, that anyone in Christ is a new creature, that God reconciled us in Christ and gave us the message of reconciliation, and that Christ was made sin for us so that we might become the righteousness of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means to be reconciled to God, using 2 Corinthians 5:18-21?
ev: Explain why Christ died for all (5:15)
Say what is true of anyone in Christ (5:17)
Explain reconciliation in 5:18-19
Explain the exchange described in 5:21

nodes.t: Separation and the temple of the living God
nodes.d: Paul warns against being unequally yoked with unbelievers, says believers are the temple of the living God, and gives promises that God will be their Father and they his sons and daughters, calling them to cleanse themselves.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says believers should not be unequally yoked with unbelievers, using 2 Corinthians 6:14-18?
ev: Name the contrasts Paul draws in 6:14-16
Say what promises are given in 6:16-18
Explain the conclusion of 7:1

nodes.t: The thorn in the flesh: power in weakness
nodes.d: Paul tells of being caught up to paradise, then of a thorn in the flesh given to keep him humble; the Lord answered his prayer by saying his grace is sufficient and his strength is made perfect in weakness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says "when I am weak, then am I strong," using 2 Corinthians 12:7-10?
ev: Say what Paul asked the Lord three times (12:8)
Quote the Lord's answer (12:9)
Explain why Paul can say he is strong when weak (12:10)

nodes.t: Two sons, two covenants: Hagar and Sarah
nodes.d: Paul uses Abraham's two sons, one by the bondwoman and one by the free woman, as an allegory of two covenants, and says believers are children of promise like Isaac and not children of the bondwoman.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul reads the story of Hagar and Sarah in Galatians 4:21-31?
ev: Say who the two sons and their mothers are (4:22-23)
Explain the two covenants named in 4:24-26
Say who Paul says we are like (4:28, 4:31)
Quote the scripture Paul cites in 4:30

nodes.t: Philippians: overview
nodes.d: Paul writes from prison to the church at Philippi about joy, the humility of Christ, pressing toward the goal, and contentment (1:1-4:23).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of Philippians and say what Paul says about joy?
ev: Say where Paul was when he wrote (1:7, 1:13)
Name the theme that recurs, rejoicing (e.g. 3:1, 4:4)

nodes.t: The mind of Christ: humbled and exalted
nodes.d: Paul urges unity and humility, pointing to Christ, who being in the form of God took the form of a servant, humbled himself to death on a cross, and was highly exalted so that every knee will bow and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the path of Christ in Philippians 2:6-11 and say how it applies to us in 2:3-5?
ev: Describe the steps of Christ's humbling (2:6-8)
Say what God did in response (2:9-11)
Say what attitude Paul asks of the Philippians (2:3-5)

nodes.t: Jesus made like his brothers
nodes.d: Jesus, made a little lower than the angels, tasted death for everyone, shared flesh and blood to destroy the devil and free those enslaved by fear of death, and became a merciful and faithful high priest able to help the tempted.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus became like his brothers according to Hebrews 2:14-18?
ev: Say why he shared flesh and blood (2:14-15)
State what kind of high priest he is (2:17)

nodes.t: 1 Peter: overview
nodes.d: 1 Peter is a letter from the apostle Peter to scattered strangers in Asia Minor, written to encourage them in suffering with the living hope, the example of Christ, holy conduct and humility under God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how 1 Peter encourages believers who suffer?
ev: Say who wrote 1 Peter and to whom
Name the main themes: hope, holiness, suffering and humility

nodes.t: Be holy: redeemed by precious blood
nodes.d: Peter calls believers to be holy as God is holy, reminds them they were redeemed by the precious blood of Christ the lamb without blemish, and says they were born again by the abiding word.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Peter says paid the price for believers, and how they should live because of it?
ev: Say what Peter says redeemed them and what it was not
Explain the call to be holy in 1:15-16
Describe what the word of the Lord does according to 1:23-25

nodes.t: The living stone and the holy priesthood
nodes.d: Peter calls Christ the living stone chosen by God, says believers are built up as a spiritual house and royal priesthood, and says they were once not a people but are now the people of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name three things Peter calls believers in 1 Peter 2:9?
ev: Explain the stone picture in 2:4-8
List the names Peter gives believers in 2:9
Say what 2:10 says changed for them

nodes.t: Christ suffered for us, an example
nodes.d: Peter says believers are called to follow the steps of Christ, who did not sin, did not revile in return, bore our sins on the tree, and brings the strayed sheep back to the Shepherd.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain both what Christ did for us and what example he left in 1 Peter 2:21-25?
ev: Describe how Christ responded when reviled
Say what Christ did on the tree in 2:24
Explain the sheep and Shepherd picture

nodes.t: Blessing, good conscience and suffering for doing good
nodes.d: Peter tells all to be of one mind and repay evil with blessing, says suffering for righteousness is blessed, and that believers should always be ready to give a reason for their hope with meekness and a good conscience.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Peter says to respond when others speak evil of us?
ev: Say how Peter tells believers to answer evil
Explain what being ready to answer for hope looks like in 3:15

nodes.t: The day of the Lord and new heavens and earth
nodes.d: Peter says the day of the Lord will come like a thief with fire dissolving the heavens and the elements, so believers should live in holiness and look for new heavens and a new earth where righteousness dwells, and grow in grace.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how Peter tells believers to live while they wait for the day of the Lord?
ev: Describe how the day of the Lord comes
Say what kind of people Peter says we ought to be in 3:11
Say what new thing believers look for in 3:13

nodes.t: Revelation: overview
nodes.d: Revelation is the revelation of Jesus Christ given to John on Patmos: letters to seven churches, a vision of the throne in heaven, the Lamb, series of seals, trumpets and bowls, and the end in the new Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline the main parts of Revelation as the book itself presents them?
ev: Say who gave the revelation and to whom
Name the main parts: churches, throne, Lamb, judgments, new heaven and earth
Say what is promised to the one who reads and keeps it in 1:3

nodes.t: The sealed scroll and the Lamb
nodes.d: John weeps that no one can open the sealed scroll until the Lion of the tribe of Juda appears as a Lamb as though slain, takes the scroll, and heaven and every creature worship him as worthy because he redeemed people from every nation by his blood.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who is worthy to open the scroll and why?
ev: Say why John wept and what was announced
Describe the Lamb and what he does
Say what the new song says about why he is worthy

nodes.t: The fall of Babylon
nodes.d: An angel announces that Babylon the great has fallen, a voice calls God's people to come out of her, and kings, merchants and sailors mourn her sudden ruin while heaven is told to rejoice.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what happens to Babylon in Revelation 18 and who mourns?
ev: Say what the voice tells God's people in 18:4
Describe who mourns and why in 18:9-19
Say what heaven is told in 18:20

nodes.t: A new heaven and a new earth
nodes.d: John sees a new heaven and new earth and the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God as a bride; God dwells with his people, wipes away every tear, and says he makes all things new, while the unbelieving have their part in the lake of fire.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what God promises in Revelation 21:1-8?
ev: Say what the voice says about God dwelling with men
List what is gone in 21:4
Say what God says in 21:5-7

nodes.t: Epilogue: I come quickly, the invitation and the warning
nodes.d: The angel and Jesus confirm the words are faithful and true, Jesus says he comes quickly with his reward and is the Alpha and Omega and the bright and morning star, the Spirit and the bride say Come and invite the thirsty, a warning is given about adding to or taking from the book, and the book ends with the grace of the Lord Jesus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how Revelation ends and what invitation it gives?
ev: Say what Jesus says about himself in 22:12-16
Quote the invitation of 22:17 in your own words
Say what the warning in 22:18-19 is about
